text:
Boston played the better hockey and lost by three. BOS finished with 2.7 expected goals to MIN's 3.53 by the total count, but at even strength the Bruins held the edge, 1.83 to 1.41, and the simulated replays gave them a 56 percent chance to win. What decided it was a Minnesota goalie who saved 1.7 goals more than his workload deserved, and a Minnesota power play that cashed both of its opportunities.

Jesper Wallstedt faced 27 shots worth 2.7 expected goals and allowed one, a first-period wrister from Tanner Jeannot at 1:53. One of the saves came on a 23 percent chance for James Hagens in the second. Michael DiPietro, at the other end, allowed three on 2.39 expected, a gap of 0.61 goals. Kirill Kaprizov tied it on a power-play snap shot at 6:11 of the second, and Quinn Hughes put MIN ahead with another man advantage goal at 12:28, off a 6 percent chance. BOS went 0 for 3 on its own power plays.

The third period belonged to Boston on paper, 1.36 to 0.59 in expected goals, yet the scoreboard moved the other way. Jared Spurgeon made it 3-1 at 3:24 on a 1 percent chance, and Kaprizov added an even-strength backhand at 18:59 for his second of the night. Wallstedt took first star, Hughes second with a goal and an assist, and the Bruins left with the better process and nothing to show for it.
